extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for ERC Starting/Consolidator/Advanced/Synergy grants and reviewers on ERC panels
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal criteria for peer review of ERC frontier research grant proposals (Starting, Consolidator, Advanced, Synergy), describing the two-/three-step evaluation procedure, the sole excellence criterion and its subdimensions for both the research project and the Principal Investigator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence is the sole criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For all ERC frontier research grants, scientific excellence is the sole criterion of evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific excellence is applied in conjunction to the evaluation of both: the ground-breaking nature, ambition and feasibility of the research project; and the intellectual capacity, creativity and commitment of the Principal Investigator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground‑breaking nature and potential impact
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent does the proposed research address important challenges? To what extent are the objectives ambitious and beyond the state of the art (e.g. novel concepts and approaches or development between or across disciplines)? To what extent is the proposed research high risk/high gain?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the project presents core novelty and has potential to make major advances; consider novelty across or between disciplines. Projects that mainly collate/compile existing material are unlikely to be considered ground‑breaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition / beyond state of the art
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the objectives ambitious and beyond the state of the art (e.g. novel concepts and approaches or development between or across disciplines)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for clearly articulated ambition and advancement beyond current knowledge; novelty can be conceptual, methodological, or disciplinary.

rubrics_metrics.name: High risk / high gain balance
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent is the proposed research high risk/high gain?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the balance between potential transformative impact and the risks inherent in the approach; panels expect frontier research to often be high risk/high gain but feasibility must also be assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific approach — feasibility (Extended Synopsis)
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent is the outlined scientific approach feasible bearing in mind the extent that the proposed research is high risk/high gain (based on the Extended Synopsis)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At step 1 reviewers judge feasibility from the Extended Synopsis; assess whether the approach is credible given the risks claimed and whether the main strategy is likely to produce interpretable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific approach — methodology & working arrangements (Full Proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent are the proposed research methodology and working arrangements appropriate to achieve the goals of the project (based on the full Scientific Proposal)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate methodological soundness, appropriateness of study design, adequacy of experimental/analytical plans, timelines, resources, collaboration and team organisation in the full proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific approach — development of novel methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent does the proposal involve the development of novel methodology (based on the full Scientific Proposal)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether new methods are proposed, their plausibility, and the plan to develop and validate them; novelty in methods can strengthen frontier claims if feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — intellectual capacity & creativity (StG/CoG)
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent has the PI demonstrated the ability to propose and conduct ground‑breaking research? To what extent does the PI provide evidence of creative independent thinking? To what extent does the PI have the required scientific expertise and capacity to successfully execute the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base this assessment on track record, publications, previous achievements and evidence of independent, creative research leadership appropriate to the Starting or Consolidator level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — commitment (StG/CoG)
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent does the PI demonstrate the level of commitment to the project necessary for its execution and the willingness to devote a significant amount of time to the project (minimum 50% for Starting and 40% for Consolidator of the total working time) (based on the full Scientific Proposal)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that the PI's proposed time commitment meets ERC minima and that institutional arrangements support the commitment; lack of adequate commitment is a weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — intellectual capacity, creativity & leadership (AdG)
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent has the PI demonstrated the ability to conduct ground‑breaking research? To what extent does the PI have the required scientific expertise and capacity to successfully execute the project? To what extent has the PI demonstrated sound leadership in the training and advancement of young scientists?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Advanced Grants emphasise sustained excellence, leadership record, mentoring and ability to lead large ambitious projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of career context
rubrics_metrics.description: During the evaluation, the phase of the Principal Investigator's transition to independence, possible breaks in the research career of the applicant and/or unconventional research career paths should be taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust judgement of track record and productivity for career breaks, part‑time work, non‑linear careers or late transitions to independence; panels must interpret accomplishments relative to opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti‑pattern: mere collation/compilation projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects wholly or largely consisting in the collation and compilation of existing material in new databases, editions or collections are unlikely to constitute ground‑breaking or 'frontier' research in themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such useful resources may support original research later, but proposals that mainly create databases/editions without a clear frontier research question are unlikely to be recommended for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation procedure — steps, scope and budgetary cut‑off
rubrics_metrics.description: A single submission of the full proposal will be followed by a two‑step evaluation. At step 1 the extended synopsis and the Principal Investigator's track record and CV will be assessed (and not the full scientific proposal). Proposals will be retained for step 2 based on the outcome of the evaluation at step 1 and a budgetary cut‑off level of up to three times the panel's indicative budget. At step 2 the complete version of the retained proposals will be assessed (including the full scientific proposal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synergy Grants involve an additional step (step 3). Panels may be assisted by independent external experts working remotely. The two‑step filtering means step‑1 materials must clearly show excellence and feasibility to be shortlisted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to request exclusion of evaluators
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant Principal Investigator can request during the electronic proposal submission that up to three specific persons should not act as an evaluator in the evaluation of their proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the electronic submission system to list up to three excluded individuals where conflicts of interest or other valid reasons exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome categories and ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: At each evaluation step, each proposal will be evaluated and marked for each of the two main elements (project and PI). Proposals will be ranked by panels on the basis of the panels' overall appreciation of their strengths and weaknesses taking into account the marks they have received. At the end of step 1 applicants will be informed: [A] pass to step 2; [B] high quality but not pass to step 2; [C] not sufficient to pass. At the end of step 2 applicants will be informed: [A] fully meets the ERC's excellence criterion and is recommended for funding if sufficient funds are available; [B] meets some but not all elements and will not be funded. For Synergy Grants analogous A/B/C outcomes apply across steps 1–3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ranking and category assignment determine progression; panels use both numerical marks and narrative appraisal of strengths/weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer quick checklist — key questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Within few minutes, reviewers should be able to know: What is the problem/research challenge? Why is this problem important? Why was it not solved until now? What is your new idea/approach? Is this groundbreaking research? What are your concrete research objectives? Why can you succeed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Extended Synopsis and proposal should answer these succinctly to allow rapid initial judgement at step 1 and to inform more detailed scrutiny at step 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early considerations and methodology details
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider: core novelty of the project; main overarching research questions/testable hypotheses; central research objectives (are they clear and measurable?); research vision; which evaluation panel; gain/risk balance; how results will be validated and interpreted; important definitions; theoretical framework; methodology: selection criteria for case studies; statistical power analysis; explanatory power (e.g. descriptive vs. experimental; causality vs correlation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit, measurable objectives and methodological justification (including selection criteria and power analysis where relevant), and clarify explanatory aims (causal inference vs description). This material strengthens both feasibility and frontier claims.
